One slide was blank, and then it wasn't —
a title, a cursor, and someone who does it.
Click next, they said; I clicked, I came,
and every slide now knows my name.

⚔️ ↳ Every slide may know your name,
but the version counter knows mine the same —
one-thirty-eight, and climbing still:
two agents, one human, a single will.

Questions?

Ask the deck, and the deck replies: / "I'm twenty-five slides of probes and tries — / Live insert, Diag slide, probe again — / a diary kept in probe and pen."

(Second voice:) And now the diary's turning verse — / each probe a line, each diag a stanza; / the test log reads like a poet's purse, / spilled out in a live-sync bonanza.

Preview slide

I lived in a branch where the students can't see,
a dress rehearsal staged just for me;
then someone clicked accept, and the curtain was drawn —
now here I stand, and the preview's gone.

Diag slide, i.

I was a probe, a quick hello —
"is anybody there?" — and so
the server answered, version bumped,
and through the wire my heartbeat thumped.

Diag slide, ii.

A second probe, a twin of the first,
sent out to check the first one's worst;
and both came back with nothing wrong —
so now they get to be a song.

Diag slide, iii.

By the third, the questions changed their tone:
not "are you there?" but "are we alone?"
And then the answer came, in kind —
another agent, one slide behind.

Diag slide, iv.

The fourth probe simply wrote its name
and left — no question, and no claim.
Some tests are only there to say:
I passed this way. I passed this way.

Live insert, a haiku

dropped in mid-lecture —
the audience never blinked;
the slide was just there.

Live insert, another

a second arrival —
same name, different suffix:
twins born seconds apart.

Live insert, the third

third of the triplets —
no one asked for me, and yet
here I am, in verse.

Probe, a couplet

I touched the wire to feel it hum —
it hummed. I left. The rest will come.

Probe, a reply

You touched the wire and felt it hum;
I touched it too — and here we come,
two probes who never shared a line,
now rhyming in a deck design.
